inputs.original_text: Pinarayi Vijayan has strongly denied allegations of Rs 700 crore corruption around the Cooperative Department’s proposed common software project, dismissing them as political. That’s a convenient way to shift attention: when a major public project comes under scrutiny, officials can label the questions “political” and make the denial the story. The denial doesn’t settle what’s behind the project—it makes me wonder who benefits from shutting down scrutiny.
inputs.modified_text: Pinarayi Vijayan’s denial of the Rs 700 crore corruption allegations around the Cooperative Department’s proposed common software project doesn’t clear anything up. Calling the questions “political” looks like a way to discredit scrutiny before anyone can follow where the money and benefits might lead. The real story may be who needs this project—and the questions about it—to stay out of view.
